papers.title: Corrigendum to "SleepEEGpy: a Python-based software integration package to organize preprocessing, analysis, and visualization of sleep EEG data" [Comput. Biol. Med. 192, (2025), 110232].
papers.summary: This corrigendum concerns errors in the paper 'SleepEEGpy: a Python-based software integration package to organize preprocessing, analysis, and visualization of sleep EEG data.'

papers.title: Novel sleep scoring method for neurodegenerative diseases: feasibility and reliability in advanced Parkinson disease.
papers.summary: The authors tested a novel sleep scoring methodology incorporating abnormal Wake, Subwake, Undifferentiated NREM, Poorly Structured N2, and abnormal REM stages in 15 advanced Parkinson disease patients and five controls, scored blinded by five raters. The method showed substantial interrater agreement (kappa = 0.75), comparable to AASM scoring (kappa = 0.73), and abnormal stages were associated with ageing and advanced PD with cognitive impairment and motor fluctuations.

papers.title: Longitudinal persistence of EEG brain fingerprints: phase and complex coherency geometry across sessions and functional states
papers.summary: Investigated the longitudinal persistence of EEG connectivity-based individual fingerprints using phase and complex coherency geometry across three cohorts spanning one month to five years, without a trained identity classifier. Alpha phasors identified 81.67% (RestCog) and 79.55% (L-FAME) of participants in rest-to-rest matching, and after five years 77.67% rank-1 identification was retained, while state changes (eyes-open/closed, task) weakened identification, distinguishing temporal persistence from robustness across functional states.

papers.title: Sleep Renormalizes Negative Emotional Generalization
papers.summary: Using a face-outcome generalization paradigm combined with fMRI and high-density EEG, the authors report that sleep selectively enhanced positive generalization while wakefulness favored negative generalization. Amygdala/limbic outcome-processing activity predicted a sleep-specific shift toward positive generalization, and sleep-spindle activity correlated with increased positive and reduced negative generalization.

papers.title: Autonomic Reactivity and EEG-defined Clusters Reveal Distinct Chronic Pain Profiles.
papers.summary: In 177 patients with chronic pain after spine surgery, the authors integrated stress-related HRV LF/HF changes with resting-state EEG features via PCA and unsupervised clustering. A nominally significant HRV-group by EEG-cluster interaction was found, with the LF/HF-decrease group reporting higher pain scores within one EEG cluster, though main effects were not significant and findings require validation.

papers.title: Eyes-open resting-state EEG microstate analysis using ratio-normalized parameters across four- and seven-class solutions in healthy controls, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: In 180 participants (60 each HC, MCI, AD), ratio-normalized eyes-open resting-state EEG microstate parameters from four- and seven-class solutions were compared. The four-class solution showed nominal MCI-versus-AD differences in visual (Microstate B) and executive (Microstate E) network engagement, but no effects survived FDR correction and the seven-class solution yielded none.

papers.title: Increased variability in visual processing in children with autism
papers.summary: Analyzed pattern-reversal VEPs in 102 typically developing and 105 autistic children aged 2-12, showing reduced N1 amplitude and lower inter-trial phase coherence (ITPC) in autism; group VEP amplitude differences vanished after accounting for ITPC. Higher ITPC was linked to resting alpha activity and, within autistic children, to better nonverbal, verbal, and language scores.

papers.title: A Retrospective Real-World Assessment of Motor Status After Stroke Using a Home-Based Brain-Computer Interface
papers.summary: Retrospective observational study of 452 stroke survivors (mean 5.4 years post-stroke, 73.7% severe impairment) using at-home EEG-based BCI (IpsiHand) therapy, with UEFM improving 4.3 points at week 12, reaching the MCID (~5.6 points) by week 16, and rising to 8.1 points at week 52.

papers.title: Human iEEG recordings during audiovisual speech violations support and extend predictive routing models
papers.summary: Using human intracranial EEG from seven presurgical epilepsy patients during an audiovisual speech paradigm, the study tested predictive routing predictions by measuring theta, alpha-beta and high-gamma power during auditory deviance, multisensory integration and McGurk incongruence. Superior temporal cortex showed increased high-gamma and decreased alpha-beta power for auditory deviance and McGurk stimuli, whereas frontal areas showed the alpha-beta decrease without a high-gamma prediction error signal and instead a strong theta-band prediction error in the McGurk condition.

papers.title: High-frequency EEG activity moderates the association between amyloid burden and tau in cognitively normal adults
papers.summary: In a pilot study of 21 cognitively normal older adults with amyloid PET (20 with tau PET), higher amyloid burden was associated with higher parietal periodic gamma power, and periodic gamma was associated with medial temporal tau only in amyloid-positive adults; gamma also moderated the amyloid-tau association (p=0.012).

papers.title: Gotta Go Fast: Intended Concentric Effort Produces Divergent Myoelectric Spectral Profiles During Fatiguing, Load-Equated Resistance Exercise.
papers.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
papers.summary: Twenty recreationally active adults performed fatiguing unilateral leg extensions at 70% 1RM under maximal intended concentric velocity (Vmax) and 50%Vmax, with wavelet-based sEMG analysis showing Vmax suppressed high-frequency bands while 50%Vmax increased power across the spectrum; profiles converged asymmetrically at task failure (rho_c=0.98 overall).

papers.title: A multimodal dataset of EEG, eye-tracking, and physiological signals during naturalistic smartphone interactions
papers.summary: Presents a publicly released multimodal BIDS-formatted dataset (OpenNeuro ds007537) of synchronized 64-channel EEG, eye-tracking, PPG, and GSR from 23 participants during 10 minutes of naturalistic smartphone use followed by a 5-minute nature-video relaxation condition, with TTL-triggered alignment and smartphone-use questionnaires.

papers.title: Diagnostic value of extending outpatient EEG to record sleep - A retrospective study.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: In 1762 outpatient EEGs extended to ~40-50 min, N2 sleep was achieved in 70.5% of patients without sleep deprivation, and sleep recording detected unique interictal epileptiform discharges in an additional 12% beyond wakefulness (total yield OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.02-1.68), with the greatest incremental gain between 20 and 30 min.

papers.title: Machine Learning Classification of Bipolar Disorder Across Mood States Using Natural Language Processing and Speech Analysis: Observational Study.
papers.summary: This observational study used LASSO-regularized logistic regression on 6373 acoustic and 211 linguistic features from speech samples of 61 bipolar disorder patients and 99 healthy controls to classify bipolar disorder and mood states. The model discriminated bipolar disorder from controls with AUC 0.916 and mood states from controls with AUC 0.805-0.874, with acoustic features comprising 96%-98% of significant features, while depressive vs euthymic state exceeded chance (AUC 0.760) and other interstate comparisons did not.

papers.title: Electrodiagnostic Classification of Sensory Neuropathies: Severity Clusters and Clinical Correlates.
papers.summary: Using hierarchical clustering of normalized sural and upper-limb SNAP amplitudes in 308 sensory neuropathy examinations, the authors defined three ordered severity classes (mild, moderate, severe) that showed monotonically increasing clinical severity and differential etiologic enrichment (immune/paraneoplastic and genetic causes in the severe class).

papers.title: Neural correlates of perceptual biases in duration perception.
papers.summary: In a duration reproduction task with EEG, frontocentral CNV depended on the previous stimulus duration regardless of sequential dependence, whereas right parietal slow potentials and P2 amplitude were associated with inter-individual differences in sequential dependence and central tendency, and a Bayesian model reproduced the observed CNV dynamics.

papers.title: Objective motion-based performance assessment in STA-MCA microanastomosis: a postprocedural debriefing platform.
papers.summary: Developed a computer vision tracking pipeline applied to microscope-recorded STA-MCA microanastomosis videos, computing motion metrics (absolute error, velocity, acceleration, jerk) plus spectral tremor power in the 6-8 Hz band, with 92.09% of footage reliably tracked across 13,183 frames. The platform flagged jerk segments above 95th-percentile thresholds and detected temporal tremor fluctuations, demonstrating feasibility of objective motion-based postprocedural self-debriefing and longitudinal performance tracking.

papers.title: Neurodevelopmental outcomes of infants evaluated for but not treated with therapeutic hypothermia: a prospective cohort study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of infants evaluated for therapeutic hypothermia based on perinatal risk factors but not meeting institutional eligibility criteria, 13 of 26 infants completing Bayley-4 assessment (50%) showed sub-normative performance in at least one developmental domain at 24 months, despite only one having acute brain injury on MRI. Higher postnatal base deficits and lactate levels, and a trend toward less sleep-wake cycling on aEEG, were observed in those with sub-normative performance.

papers.title: An integrative view of human nociceptor diversity: from microneurography to molecular identity.
papers.summary: This review integrates microneurography-defined biophysical hallmarks of human nociceptors (e.g., activity-dependent slowing, recovery cycle signatures, following frequency) with patch-clamp, Patch-seq, transcriptomic atlases, and computational modeling to link nerve fiber function to molecular identity and ion channel mechanisms in neuropathic pain.

papers.title: Role of reverse remodelling in recurrence of atrial fibrillation after patient-tailored catheter ablation.
papers.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
papers.summary: In patient-specific left atrial models from 15 AF patients, targeted in-silico ablation of re-entrant drivers acutely terminated AF in all models, and recurrence after ablation fell progressively with increasing electrical reverse remodelling (55% at 0%, 36.7% at 50%, 5% at 100%), reaching 0% with full structural and electrical reverse remodelling.

papers.title: Atypical Pediatric Epilepsy: A Narrative Review of Classification, Diagnosis, and Emerging Therapeutics.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes classification, epidemiology, etiology, and emerging precision therapies for atypical pediatric epilepsies, including Lennox-Gastaut, Dravet, infantile epileptic spasms, and FIRES. It emphasizes the diagnostic gap from phenotypic overlap, EEG limitations, and barriers to timely genetic testing, and highlights a shift toward targeted pharmacologic, antisense oligonucleotide, gene therapy, and neuromodulation approaches.

papers.title: Restitution properties during ventricular fibrillation and the effects of cardiac pacing location on ventricular electrophysiology in the rabbit heart.
papers.summary: Using Langendorff-perfused rabbit hearts and monophasic action potential recordings from left ventricular apex and base, this study tested whether pacing site and prior activation history affect ventricular repolarization. Steady-state APD, effective refractory period, and conduction time restitution were largely independent of pacing location, whereas during early ventricular fibrillation APD showed short-term cardiac memory dependent on preceding diastolic interval and APD for about the first 30 beats before these relationships deteriorated.

papers.title: Atypical Atrial Flutter From Lipomatous Hypertrophy of the Interatrial Septum in a Procedure-Naive Patient.
keywords: lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum
papers.summary: This case report describes an 86-year-old procedure-naive man with new-onset atypical atrial flutter at 280 beats/min in whom intracardiac echocardiography identified lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum and electroanatomic mapping localized earliest focal activation to the superior posteroseptal right atrium at the LHIS site. Radiofrequency ablation terminated the flutter and rendered it noninducible, supporting LHIS as an isolated arrhythmogenic substrate.

papers.title: Reported Life-Threatening Polymorphic Ventricular Arrhythmia With Torsade-Like Morphology in a Patient With Gordon Syndrome and Hyperkalaemia.
papers.summary: Reports a 37-year-old woman with genetically confirmed CUL3-related Gordon syndrome who developed hyperkalaemia after a three-week interruption of bendroflumethiazide, with a reported self-terminating torsade-like polymorphic ventricular arrhythmia, and subsequently received an extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator after thiazide resumption improved potassium control. The authors note that the original rhythm tracing was unavailable and that the temporal association does not establish causation.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
